caption: How an APRS position gets onto the map: your tracker beacons a packet on the national 144.390 MHz channel, hilltop digipeaters relay it, an iGate pushes it onto the internet, and friends watch your dot move on aprs.fi.
spoken: A path diagram: a handheld tracker beacons its GPS position on 144.390 MHz, a digipeater relays the packet, an internet gateway called an iGate forwards it onto the internet, and the position appears as a moving dot on a map site.
